subject: surgery
title: Midgut Volvulus, Anorectal Malformation and NEC

steps.tx: Twisting of the whole midgut around its narrow mesenteric base is **midgut volvulus**. Blood flow to most of the bowel is cut at once. Bilious vomiting in a newborn with a tender distended abdomen means theatre immediately. The duodenum fails to cross the midline on contrast study, and the corkscrew sign shows bowel winding around the artery.
steps.say: Midgut volvulus twists the whole midgut and cuts its blood flow, needing immediate theatre.

steps.tx: At surgery the volvulus is untwisted anticlockwise, remembered as **turn back the clock**. Warm packs let questionable bowel declare itself before resection decisions. A second look operation may be planned when viability is doubtful. The twist is usually clockwise, so untwisting anticlockwise is correct, and the Ladd bands over the duodenum are divided at the same operation.
steps.say: Volvulus is untwisted anticlockwise at surgery, with a second look when viability is doubtful.

steps.tx: Failure of normal anal canal development at birth forms an **anorectal malformation**. The level of the defect and fistula type guide reconstruction. Associated spinal, urinary and cardiac anomalies are common and must be screened. Invertogram imaging has largely given way to contrast and examination under anaesthesia to define the level.
steps.say: Anorectal malformation reflects failed anal development and needs screening for associated anomalies.

steps.tx: Inflammatory death of bowel wall in premature newborns is **necrotising enterocolitis**. Feeding intolerance, distension and bloody stools develop in sick preterm babies. Gas within the bowel wall on films confirms the diagnosis. Gas inside the bowel wall, pneumatosis intestinalis, with portal vein gas marks advanced disease needing senior review.
steps.say: Necrotising enterocolitis kills bowel wall in premature babies and shows gas in the wall.

steps.tx: Free air and fixed dilated loops in necrotising enterocolitis indicate **perforation**. Most babies are managed with gut rest, antibiotics and support without surgery. Perforation or deterioration despite treatment forces operation. A fixed loop that stays in the same place on serial films worries surgeons as much as free air does.
steps.say: Perforation in necrotising enterocolitis forces surgery, while most babies manage without it.

steps.tx: Short bowel after massive resection leads to dependence on intravenous feeding, called **short bowel syndrome**. Gradual bowel adaptation over months reduces this dependence in many children. Multidisciplinary nutrition teams manage growth carefully. The remaining bowel adapts over one to two years, growing wider and longer, and many children wean off intravenous feeds in that window.
steps.say: Short bowel syndrome after massive resection needs long term nutrition team care.

steps.tx: Colostomy before definitive anorectal reconstruction protects the repair and is called a **defunctioning stoma**. It also lets distal imaging define the fistula anatomy precisely. Closure follows once reconstruction heals. Contrast injected through the stoma, a distal loopogram, maps the fistula before the pull through operation.
steps.say: A defunctioning stoma protects anorectal reconstruction and defines fistula anatomy.

steps.tx: Bowel continence after anorectal repair depends on sphincter quality and defect level, termed **functional prognosis**. Low defects usually achieve good control, high defects often need bowel management programmes. Honest counselling helps families plan. Sacral bony defects predict worse continence, so a plain sacral film is part of the early workup.
steps.say: Functional prognosis after anorectal repair depends on defect level and sphincter quality.

steps.tx: Any newborn failing to pass meconium in twenty four hours needs evaluation for **mechanical obstruction**. Hirschsprung disease, atresia and meconium plug head the list. Rectal examination and plain films start the workup. About one in three term babies who pass no meconium by 48 hours has Hirschsprung disease or an atresia.
steps.say: Failure to pass meconium in a day needs evaluation for obstruction or Hirschsprung disease.
